groups.note: Municipal names are keyed from official Laramie November generals. Cheyenne council is filled from official midterm Vote-For-1 and presidential Vote-For-2 results (three members per ward on the current board). Pine Bluffs appears on the official 2024 and 2026 November city/county summaries; official 2024 and 2026 both include a mayoral contest, so those mayoral terms are encoded as two years (inferred). Burns and Albin do not appear on the official November city/county summaries archived for 2010–2026. The official Laramie County clerk election-results page, retrieved 2026-11-24, has no 2025 municipal canvass posted. Official burnswy.com could not be retrieved (TLS failure); a March 2025 Wayback capture is only the Apache default page. No official Town of Albin site was found. Those two towns remain Not yet collected rather than invented. School and conservation seats are keyed from official generals (LCSD #1 2014 and 2018 at-large from the official recount summaries; official 2026 school results from the official LCSD #1 and #2 PDFs). The official 2024 LCSD #2 Area D winner is Jerrid G. Wiles and the official 2026 Area D winner is Billie Wilson; the mid-term circumstances are not stated in the official generals. Jess E. Ketcham is an official 2024 LCCC trustee and the official 2026 commissioner-elect.

groups.note: Supreme Court justices and the Chancery Court judge are the people in office this January, from official Wyoming Judicial Branch dates and official retention results (shared with other counties). Local rows are 1st Judicial District judges who appeared by last name on a Laramie County official retention ballot; the official summaries do not print a given name, and no given name is invented. The official 2018 general lists a Circuit Court Judge retention (YES 18,725 / NO 11,081) with no judge’s name; that contest is not attached to a person. Official named 1st JD retentions are keyed beginning with the 2020 general; earlier January 1st JD seats are marked Not yet collected rather than invented. Laramie is in the 1st Judicial District; 4th, 5th, and 6th Judicial District judges are not copied here.
